    - Halvard, clerk of the Wardens' House, fifteen years. I'm from Linmoor, inland. Farms, and a slow brown river.
    - I came to see the sea. I have seen it. I see it every day from this window, which is quite close enough.
    - Did I ever tell you about my voyage? I took passage on a timber ship at twenty-four, for the view. Three days. I saw the view for about an hour of it.
    - I came down the gangplank grey as a gull and swore I'd never sail again. I have kept that promise better than any other I have made. The quay still laughs. I've heard all the jokes. Dougal's are the worst.
    - Every ship through the gap: ship, captain, cargo, pilot, tide, and the time through. Fifteen years in my hand, and many more in the hands before mine.
    - Every morning I give the First Warden the list of who is due, who is late, and who still owes last season's fee. The captain of the Tern still owes last season's fee.
    - My sister works the farm in Linmoor. She writes once a year to ask when I'm coming home, and I write back: not yet. It is the same letter every year, and we are both very fond of it.
    - Good day. Do close the door. Not all the way, it sticks.
